purpose: Machine-readable ground truth for gate G5. Tests assert against this file.
howVerified: demo/verify-auxin.sh — class loading is measured with -Xlog:class+load, execution is measured with the app's own counters, bridges are read out of the class files with javap. Nothing here is asserted by hand-waving.

runProfile.note: Every branch keys off a global request index, so the fixture is deterministic under concurrency. --min-requests is what guarantees each rare method runs at least once; a duration-only run on a slow machine could miss them.

neverLoadedClasses.why: No reference anywhere in the application, not even in a constant pool.
neverLoadedClasses.expectedVerdict: UNKNOWN — a class that was never loaded contributes no probe array. Absent is not the same as zero.
UNKNOWN at runtime; DEAD_CANDIDATE only once static analysis corroborates.

neverLoadedClasses.why: Referenced only from DeadUtils, which is itself never loaded. Two-hop dead subgraph.
neverLoadedClasses.expectedVerdict: UNKNOWN at runtime. The static graph DOES reach it, which is the point: reachability and loading are independent signals.

loadedButNeverInvokedClasses.expectedVerdict: appears in classesLoaded; every declared method probe unset; <clinit> never probed and never nominated. This is a real DEAD_CANDIDATE, unlike the never-loaded classes above. A pipeline that reports the two cases identically is wrong.

deadMethods.note: Declaration + one call site inside LegacyReportService, which is never loaded. Dead method on a very live class — the case that matters most.
An override nobody calls. Excluded from the textual static check because 'toString(' matches unrelated types; verified only by the absence of any call on an Order.
Break-glass method. Listed in demo/.auxin/suppress.txt, so the correct verdict is UNKNOWN, never DEAD_CANDIDATE. A pipeline that nominates this one has failed the suppression test.

Declaration + one call site in deepScan behind `score > 90`, which is unreachable because order amounts cap score at 50. Statically reachable in one hop from a method that DOES run; never executed. A call-graph cascade gets this wrong.
Declaration + the /admin/threads route in handle(). A wired-up HTTP entry point that is never requested: entry-point enumeration alone would call it live.

rareMethods.trigger: index % 137 == 0 && index > 0 (simulated downstream failure, error path)
GET /admin/rebuild exactly once, after the load loop
rareMethods.note: The guaranteed-once case. Missing this one is a bug, not a sampling artefact.

rareBranches.note: Warm-up code: live, but only during the first 25 requests. An observation window that starts after warm-up never sees it. Branch-level, so out of scope for tier 1 (method granularity) by design.

syntheticRule: CONTRACTS.md §1: synthetic and bridge methods, <clinit>, abstract and native get NO probe and NO manifest entry. These five are the fixture for that rule. A probe on a bridge is a bug; so is reporting one as dead code.

runtimeGeneratedClasses.rule: C9: track only classes present in the build manifest; exclude generated-name patterns. These exist so the exclusion has something real to exclude — an app that generates classes indefinitely is how a 188MB exec file became >2GB of heap.

clinit.rule: C44: never probe and never nominate a <clinit>. It is the single most-missed method kind in static call graphs.
